article.articleHeadline: Nebezpečná nákaza se u ženy, která cestovala po Ugandě, nepotvrdila
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dangerous infection in a woman who had traveled around Uganda was not confirmed.
article.articleSummary: On 2 August 2026, a woman hospitalized at Prague Bulovka hospital after returning from Uganda did not have a confirmed dangerous infection. The Czech Health Ministry said samples were overnight evaluated by the Robert Koch Institute in Berlin, testing for tropical diseases including Ebola. The patient remains under care as doctors refine the diagnosis, with results pending. The infection probability was low; she had traveled in Uganda about 700 kilometers from the Ebola outbreak origin in the Democratic Republic of Congo and spent two weeks on a guided tour with no contact with locals. She returned 29 July and was transferred from the infectious disease clinic in Hradec Králové to Bulovka on 1 August, with staff wearing protective gear. Uganda's Ebola outbreak had ended after 42 days with 20 cases and 2 deaths; most cases were in Congo, where totals exceed 3,500 and 1,556 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダを旅行していた女性の危険な感染症は確認されなかった
triage.triage_reason: チェコで隔離されたエボラ疑い症例は検査の結果否定されており、実際の感染事例ではないため公衆衛生上の重大性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はチェコにおけるエボラ疑い症例の否定であり、DRCやウガンダのエボラ流行状況は背景情報として言及されているのみで記事の主題国ではないため、verified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: China's third medical expert team arrives in DR Congo to support Ebola response
article.articleSummary: On Aug. 1, 2026, Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, received China’s third medical expert team assigned to the Ebola response. Members arrived to support the DRC’s efforts to strengthen defenses against the Ebola epidemic, according to Xinhua. The arrival underscores ongoing international assistance to the outbreak response and expands local capacity to address transmission through expert guidance and technical support. By deploying a third team, China signals continued commitment to aiding the DRC’s public health measures in confronting Ebola. The report centers on the arrival and intended role of the team in strengthening defense against Ebola, highlighting international cooperation in epidemic containment.

triage.headline_ja: 中国の第3次医療専門家チームがコンゴ民主共和国に到着、エボラ対応を支援
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱のアウトブレイクに対し国際支援（中国の第3次専門家チーム派遣）が継続しており、公衆衛生上の深刻性と国際的関心が高いためフルRRA対象とする。
triage.notes: 記事は中国からの医療支援チーム派遣に関するものであり、エボラ発生自体はDRCで継続中。中国は支援国であり発生国ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebolagyanúval szállítottak kórházba egy Ugandából hazatért nőt Csehországban
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A woman who had returned from Uganda was transported to a hospital in the Czech Republic with suspected Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Sudden suspected Ebola virus disease in a woman returning from Uganda was transported in a specialized isolation biobox from Hradec Králové University Hospital to Prague's Bulovka University Hospital infectious diseases clinic. The Czech Health Ministry says the likelihood of confirmed Ebola is low and the public faces no danger. The patient, a tourist who visited Uganda with a route roughly 700 kilometers from the outbreak epicenters, spent most time in national parks and reportedly had no contact with locals during the organized trip. She developed fever and proactively informed doctors by telephone before seeking care, enabling pre-emptive precautions. Some samples have been sent to the Robert Koch Institute in Berlin; results were expected by Sunday morning. The situation is part of broader warnings as Ebola and other hemorrhagic fevers, along with dengue, circulate in border regions of Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, prompting travel advisories from the Czech Foreign Ministry.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダから帰国した女性がエボラ疑いでチェコの病院に搬送
triage.triage_reason: エボラ疑い例として異常性は高いが、確定診断前でありチェコ保健省も公衆衛生リスクは低いと評価。患者は現地住民との接触なしとされ、対象国（DRC等）での実際の感染確認事例ではないため続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 本事例はチェコ共和国内での疑い患者に関するもので、実際の感染発生国はウガンダ（対象国外）。DRCは国境地域における出血熱・デング熱流行の背景情報として言及されているのみで、記事の主題国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。確定診断結果（Robert Koch Instituteでの検査）待ちの状況であり、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: СЗО съобщи за бързото разпространение на епидемията от Ебола в Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO reports rapid spread of the Ebola outbreak in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is accelerating, described by the WHO as the largest ever recorded in the country. By end of July, DRC reported 3,605 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality ~44%). The surge affects regions with unstable governance and severely limited health infrastructure. In the latest reporting week, 567 new cases and 296 deaths were recorded, indicating exceptionally rapid spread. Health workers continue to be affected, with 151 infections including 44 deaths. The WHO warns of sustained transmission and a rising case burden, urging a substantial scale-up of response measures to control the outbreak. Figures cited from a WHO press release via Le Figaro confirm ongoing circulation in affected areas of the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、コンゴでのエボラ流行が急速に拡大していると発表
triage.triage_reason: WHOが史上最大規模と評価するエボラ流行がDRCで急速に拡大しており、致死率も高く、国際的拡大リスクと渡航・貿易制限リスクを含むIHR基準に複数該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: WHOはこれをDRC史上最大のエボラ流行と位置づけており、医療従事者への感染拡大や統治不安定地域での対応困難も指摘されている。続報でのWHO正式リスク評価の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Man Swats Drain Fly Then Rubs Eye, Ends Up Losing An Eyeball To Severe Infection
article.articleSummary: In China, a man swatted a drain/moth fly that landed on his lower left eyelid and rubbed his eye, initially diagnosed as seasonal conjunctivitis. His condition rapidly worsened, with a Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection causing severe tissue damage around the eye and leading to enucleation of the left eyeball. Drain flies breed in damp, dirty areas and can carry bacteria such as E. coli, Salmonella, and P. aeruginosa. A separate report describes an eight-year-old girl with a digestive tract infection from moth fly larvae, likely after water splashing from a sink or toilet contaminated bathroom surfaces and exposure to her toothbrush/cup. Ophthalmologist Li of Peking University People’s Hospital notes two eye routes: the fly entering the eye and transferring bacteria/debris, or being crushed by hands. Management includes flushing the eye with artificial tears or saline, applying antibiotic drops if available, and seeking urgent care if pain, redness, or vision changes persist.

article.articleHeadline: Kolom Pakar: Virus Paru di PIR PDPI
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Expert Column: Lung Virus at PIR PDPI.
article.articleSummary: At the Pertemuan Ilmiah Respirasi (PIR) of the Indonesian Pulmonology Association (PDPI) in Cirebon, on August 1, 2026, Prof. Tjandra delivered a plenary lecture to about 300 attendees from West Java and neighboring regions. He outlined eight globally relevant respiratory viruses that could already be present in Indonesia: avian influenza, seasonal influenza, Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV), Nipah virus disease, hantavirus infection, COVID-19, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV). The talk underscores the rising burden of pulmonary diseases in West Java and stresses that future pandemics are possible, though the timing and causative agents are unknown. The article does not report laboratory-confirmed outbreaks, infection sources, or specifics on imported/exported cases. The emphasis remains on preparedness for viral respiratory diseases as a looming pandemic risk rather than on a particular outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Pemkab Deli Serdang Genjot Eliminasi TBC, Targetkan 100 Ribu Kasus Terdeteksi - merdeka.com
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deli Serdang Regency Government Accelerates TB Elimination, Targets 100,000 Detected Cases
article.articleSummary: Deli Serdang Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia, launches an accelerated TB elimination campaign from August 1 to October 31, 2026, targeting the detection of at least 100,000 TB cases through integrated Free Health Check (Cek Kesehatan Gratis, CKG). The plan uses 480 loci, each screening about 100 people (initial ~48,000 screened) with a goal of 100,000 detections to hasten elimination by 2030 as part of the Generasi Emas 2045 initiative. Collaboration includes private hospitals/clinics and village heads under district authorities; focus areas include Percut Sei Tuan, notably Sei Rotan village, due to higher TB incidence. Mobile X-ray-equipped service cars will conduct door-to-door screening, emphasizing contacts and household contacts. The program integrates CKG, TB elimination, and the Three Million Homes (Tiga Juta Rumah) initiative, and provides comprehensive support: nutrition, housing improvements (bedah rumah), and patient accompaniment to ensure treatment completion while reducing stigma.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in DRC the fastest growing in the history of the virus
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Bundibugyo strain) is the fastest-growing on record, with 3,360 confirmed cases across five eastern provinces and 1,487 deaths (case fatality ~45%). Declared May 15, the outbreak is unfolding in Ituri province (Bunia, Rwampara health zones) amid insecurity, mining activity and high population density. Congo’s response includes strengthened surveillance via community liaison officers, more than 20 Ebola treatment centres, and local laboratories for testing. As of July 15, about 20 people had been enrolled in early July clinical trials for a Bundibugyo-strain vaccine, with results possible over the next four months; there is no standard treatment. Uganda has sent experts to border regions Tchomia and Kasenyi; it recently declared its own outbreak over, underscoring cross-border cooperation.

article.articleHeadline: Januari-Juli 2026, Sebaran Rubella di Bantul Meningkat, Dinkes Catat 35 Kasus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: January–July 2026, spread of rubella in Bantul has increased, Health Department records 35 cases.
article.articleSummary: Rubella cases in Bantul Regency, Yogyakarta Special Region, Indonesia rose to 35 between January 1 and July 30, 2026, up from 14 cases the previous year, according to the Bantul Health Department. Most infections affect preschool children; officials say there is no epidemiological linkage between cases. Common symptoms include fever and maculopapular rash. To curb transmission, authorities emphasize full Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccination per schedule: at 9 months, 18 months, and in first grade. MR vaccination has reached 8,410 infants, 9,418 under-two children, and 12,710 School Immunization Month (BIAS) participants, with vaccines distributed to health centers (Puskesmas) ahead of BIAS phase I in August and phase II in November. Rubella vaccination also aims to protect pregnant women from infection and prevent congenital rubella syndrome, which can cause fetal heart defects, hearing loss, or cataracts. In addition to vaccination, households are urged to maintain hygiene, including handwashing, cough etiquette, and nutritious food.

article.articleHeadline: ВОЗ предупредила о стремительном распространении Эболы
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO warned of the rapid spread of Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading rapidly. By 30 July 2026, the DRC reported 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths, with a case fatality rate above 40%. The outbreak, the largest ever recorded in the country, began on 15 May and is driven by a new Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain for which no licensed vaccine exists yet. The most promising vaccine candidate is under development by Hilleman Laboratories, a Singapore-based company. The World Health Organization warns sustained transmission and a rising case-load indicate a worsening epidemic. Ebola is not transmitted via the airborne route (unlike influenza or COVID-19). Ebola virus disease is a rare but extremely dangerous viral illness, with mortality historically ranging from 25% to 90%.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mumbai Monsoon Diseases 2026: The monsoon has become the disease season in Mumbai! Dengue, malaria, and leptospirosis cases rise in BMC data—find out how many cases were reported.
article.articleSummary: Between January 1 and July 14, 2026, Mumbai recorded rising monsoon-related illnesses, with dengue, malaria, leptospirosis, and chikungunya increasing versus last year, according to Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) data. Ongoing heavy rains and waterlogging create breeding grounds for Aedes and Anopheles mosquitoes and for leptospira, heightening infection risk. Dengue cases are highest in South Mumbai, especially in D Ward (Malabar Hill, Walkeshwar, Tardeo, Girgaum); C and E wards also report several cases. The report does not provide exact counts. Public health advice urges residents to eliminate standing water, regularly clean water containers (coolers, pots, tanks), wear long sleeves, and use mosquito repellent. Seek urgent medical care for fever with body pains, low platelets, or persistent vomiting. With monsoon continuing, experts warn that mosquito-borne disease risk may rise further.

article.articleHeadline: Ebolar da Congo ke fuskanta ta kama hanyar zama mafi muni a tarihi- WHO
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is on track to become the worst in history - WHO.
article.articleSummary: As of 2 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could become the deadliest in history if not contained, according to WHO. Since first reported on 15 May, transmission has spread to five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, and Tshopo—and has reached 49 health facilities. Total cases are 3,605, with 1,587 deaths. In the latest reporting period, 567 new infections and 296 deaths were recorded, the largest weekly toll since the outbreak began. Authorities have struggled to halt transmission from Mongbwalu in Ituri over the past two months. The unfolding outbreak underlines the need for intensified public health measures to curb spread across the affected regions.

article.articleHeadline: Why Uganda seems to be winning the battle against Ebola as virus spreads in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak in Ituri, centered on Bunia, is the second-worst on record, with official deaths surpassing 1,500 since the May declaration and the virus spreading faster than in prior outbreaks. Uganda reports a contrasting trajectory: 20 cases and 2 deaths, with the last patient discharged about two weeks ago; authorities credited preparedness and rapid response. Of Uganda's 20 cases, 15 originated from DR Congo; the first two may have been misidentified initially. The Ugandan government opened an Ebola treatment centre at Mulago Hospital in Kampala and closed the border with DR Congo to limit cross-border transmission, while quarantining more than 6,000 contacts. In DR Congo, surveillance is hampered by insecurity in Ituri, with M23-held areas complicating response. The Bundibugyo strain behind the current outbreak complicates detection. The outbreak marks the 17th Ebola event in DR Congo since discovery; Uganda’s prior experiences and open outbreak reporting aided containment.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: The Ebola epidemic in Congo is the most severe in history.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization reports the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the most severe in the country’s history. By the end of July 2026, 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality rate ≈44%) have been recorded. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, declared on May 15, 2026, which has surpassed the 2018–2020 outbreak (about 3,500 cases and ~2,300 deaths). There is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo; vaccines are under development in the United Kingdom and Singapore. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids. The WHO warned of accelerated transmission, citing 567 cases and 296 deaths in the most recent week. The epicenter is Ituri Province in northeast DRC, bordering South Sudan and Uganda, with spread to North and South Kivu, where areas are controlled by the M23 group. Additional cases include 20 in Uganda, one in France, and two DRC cases treated in Germany.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Becomes Country's Largest Ever, WHO Warns of Rapid Spread
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is now the country’s largest Ebola outbreak on record. As of 30 July 2026, 3,605 cases and 1,587 deaths have been confirmed across five provinces and 49 health zones, with Ituri reporting 3,176 cases and 1,311 deaths. The outbreak has surpassed the 2018–2020 episode (3,317 cases); the latest week added 567 cases and 296 deaths. Thirty-three health zones remain active. Ituri began in Mongbwalu and has spread to North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo. A total of 17,863 contacts have been identified; 651 recovered; 151 healthcare workers infected (44 deaths, 68 recoveries). Insecurity, displacement and cross-border movement hinder response; Uganda ended its Bundibugyo outbreak on 28 July, but risk remains nearby. No vaccines or specific treatments exist; control relies on isolation, contact tracing and safe burials. WHO urges stronger community engagement and cross-border coordination.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : une nouvelle zone de santé touchée dans la Tshopo, le gouvernement renforce les mesures de surveillance
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: a new health zone hit in Tshopo, the government strengthens surveillance measures.
article.articleSummary: New Ebola virus disease outbreak update in the Democratic Republic of Congo: a new health zone, Kabondo, in Tshopo province, is now affected, bringing the total number of affected health zones to 49 of 140 across five provinces (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uele). Two months after the declaration of the 17th Ebola epidemic, cases continue to emerge in multiple regions. Government actions focus on strengthening medical care access, including the declaration of free care in Ituri, expanding on-the-ground surveillance, and reinforcing entry-point health surveillance and other control points. A report on community awareness and mobilization measures was also presented. The response faces challenges, notably health worker strikes in Ituri and ongoing insecurity, with some treatment centers attacked by armed groups. Authorities pursue vaccine development for Bundibugyo Ebola strain and reaffirm commitment to mobilize resources and address health workers’ demands.

article.articleHeadline: AFRICOM chief confirms US support for Laikipia Ebola quarantine facility
article.articleSummary: Ebola quarantine facility established at Laikipia Air Base in Kenya; AFRICOM confirms U.S. involvement in providing support while insisting the initiative was public health-led, not a military operation, with public health authorities and the Kenyan government in charge. Seven Americans, who worked in the Democratic Republic of Congo during the Ebola outbreak, are quarantining in Kenya after returning home; Samaritan’s Purse says they are under a 21‑day quarantine and have not developed symptoms. Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale had disputed reports that the seven were quarantined at the Laikipia site. The project previously faced a High Court halt and renewed protests in Nanyuki amid concerns about transparency, public participation, and Kenya’s role in the U.S. Ebola preparedness plan. The facility is described as part of Kenya’s public health preparedness and is not exclusive to U.S. citizens; questions remain about the agreement and agency responsibilities.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in Congo becomes country's largest on record
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo strain Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the nation’s largest on record. As of 30 July, 3,605 cases and 1,587 deaths were reported to the World Health Organization, up 13% from a week earlier. The crude fatality rate is about 44%. In the latest week, 567 new confirmed cases and 296 deaths were recorded—the highest weekly totals since the outbreak began. The outbreak has spread from Mongbwalu in Ituri into five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo. Response is hampered by political instability, displacement and cross-border movement. Uganda declared its Bundibugyo outbreak over on 28 July, but remains vulnerable to imports from eastern Congo. WHO urges heightened surveillance and scaled-up response to outpace transmission and prevent regional spread.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak is worsening in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo worsens, with ongoing transmission, rising mortality, and expanding geographic spread. As of 30 July 2026, there are 3,605 laboratory-confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths. Last week recorded 567 new cases and 296 deaths—the heaviest weekly toll since the outbreak began, signaling unprecedented transmission. Factors driving spread include insecurity, population displacement, and cross-border movements that hamper response and raise regional risk. National authorities, WHO, and partners are implementing key control measures, but intensified, multi-sector operations are urgently needed to curb transmission. Bundibugyo virus is an Ebola virus species that causes Bundibugyo virus disease; the outbreak remains centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with an elevated risk of cross-border spread.

triage.headline_ja: WHO：コンゴ民主共和国でブンディブギョウイルス（エボラ）の流行が悪化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ（ブンディブギョウウイルス）の症例・死亡が急増し、流行開始以来最悪の週間報告、越境拡大リスクも指摘されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大事案。
triage.notes: 累計3,605例（確定）、死亡1,587例、致死率が非常に高い。前週だけで567新規症例・296死亡は流行開始以来最多。治安悪化・住民移動・越境移動が対応を阻害し地域的リスクを高めている。多分野の強化対応が急務とされ、外部支援の必要性が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: WHO reports DRC's largest-ever Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the country’s largest Ebola outbreak on record, with 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality ratio 44%) reported as of July 30. The outbreak spans five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo—and 49 health zones, after starting in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri. Epidemiological week 30 recorded 567 new cases and 296 deaths, signaling sustained transmission. Insecurity, population displacement, high mobility and cross-border movement are hindering containment and surveillance. The Congolese government, with WHO and partners, has intensified response but urgent scale-up is required. Neighbouring countries are strengthening regional surveillance; Uganda declared its Bundibugyo outbreak over after 42 days without local transmission. Authorities will expand surveillance, treatment and community response to curb further spread within DRC and across borders.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、コンゴ民主共和国で過去最大のブンディブギョ・エボラ流行を報告
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)流行が発生し、致死率44%、5州49保健地区に拡大、越境リスクもあることからIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダは同株の流行を42日間の伝播なしで終息宣言済みのため、DRCのみを対象国とした。治安不安・住民移動が封じ込めを困難にしており、越境拡大リスクが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ririn Ekawati Ajak Orang Tua Cegah DBD di ASEAN Dengue Day 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ririn Ekawati Urges Parents to Prevent Dengue Fever on ASEAN Dengue Day 2026
article.articleSummary: Ririn Ekawati, accompanied by her daughter, spoke at the ASEAN Dengue Day 2026 climax at the National Library of Indonesia, urging parents to prevent dengue fever by building simple, consistent home habits from an early age. The event, organized with Enesis Group’s Soffell brand and Indonesia’s Ministry of Health, the DKI Jakarta Health Office, and the Jakarta Education Office, highlighted family roles in promoting healthy living and dengue awareness. A preceding roadshow educated several Jakarta elementary schools (SDN 03 and 05 Tanah Tinggi; SDN 20 Utan Kayu Selatan; SDN 02 Mampang Prapatan) on the PSN 3M+ approach: drain water-holding containers, tightly close storage, recycle items that can breed mosquitoes, and protect against bites. The campaign, themed Indonesia as a pioneer of a dengue-free ASEAN, seeks to embed prevention in schools and homes and advance the Indonesia Zero Deaths from dengue by 2030. Dengue data: 2025 ~161,000 cases and >600 deaths; mid-2026 ~50,000 cases and >100 deaths; highest deaths in ages 5–14; most cases in 15–44.

triage.headline_ja: リリン・エカワティ、ASEANデングデー2026で親にデング熱予防を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: デング熱の啓発イベントに関する記事だが、記載されている感染統計（2025年約16.1万例・600人超死亡、2026年半ばで約5万例・100人超死亡）は継続的な流行状況を示しており、既知の風土病的拡大として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事は主に啓発キャンペーンの報道であり、新規の異常な事象ではないが、インドネシアにおけるデング熱の高い罹患・死亡数のデータが含まれるため、疫学的動向として注視の価値あり。

article.articleHeadline: Nyaralás után a kórházban kötött ki, veszélyes fertőzés gyanúja merült fel az Ugandában kiránduló nőnél
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: After a vacation, she ended up in hospital; suspicion of a dangerous infection arose in the woman touring Uganda.
article.articleSummary: Suspected infection of a highly dangerous pathogen arises in a Czech woman returning from Uganda. On 2026-08-02, paramedics transported her in a specialized biological isolation unit to the Infectious Diseases Department of Prague’s Bulovka University Hospital; the Czech Ministry of Health says the likelihood of a true dangerous infection is low and the public remains at no increased risk. The patient traveled as a tourist to Uganda, visiting areas about 700 kilometers from the Ebola outbreak epicenter and spending much time in national parks with no direct contact with locals under an organized itinerary. She presented with fever and had notified doctors by phone about recent international travel, enabling early precautions for staff and residents. Some samples are being sent to the Berlin Robert Koch Institute for further testing. The report also notes dengue and other viral hemorrhagic fevers as differential diagnoses; travel to Uganda and the Uganda-DRC border regions is cautioned by the Czech Foreign Ministry.

triage.headline_ja: 休暇後に入院、ウガンダを旅行していた女性に危険な感染症の疑いが浮上
triage.triage_reason: エボラ疑いの症例だが、チェコ保健省は真の感染の可能性は低いとしており、確定診断ではないため続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 本記事はチェコ人女性の疑い症例（ウガンダ旅行後）に関する報道であり、確定患者ではない。ウガンダおよびDRCはエボラ流行の背景情報として言及されているが、対象国であるDRCについても本症例の直接的な発生地とは言えず、記事の主題（患者発生・診断）はチェコで進行中のため、対象国リストに合致する『実際の発生国』としては該当なしと判断した。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie causée par la souche Bundibugyo est "désormais la plus importante épidémie d'Ebola jamais signalée en RDC", signale l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain is now the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the DRC, according to the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has become the largest ever reported, according to the WHO. As of July 30, 2026, 3,605 laboratory-confirmed cases have been recorded across five provinces, with 1,587 deaths and 651 recoveries, yielding a case fatality rate of 44%. The epidemic is intensifying with sustained transmission and rising caseloads and fatalities. Vaccination and treatment efforts are underway: Oxford University has administered its experimental vaccine against Bundibugyo to one volunteer, and Russia has signaled readiness to scale up production of a vaccine. In early July, the DRC, with support from Africa CDC and WHO, launched a clinical trial evaluating two experimental treatments for the new Ebola strain. Ongoing outbreak activity continues to drive international collaboration.

triage.headline_ja: ブンディブギョ株によるエボラ流行、DRCで過去最大規模の流行と WHO が発表
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるブンディブギョ株エボラ流行がWHOにより過去最大規模と報告され、5州で3,605例・死亡1,587例・致死率44%と深刻な公衆衛生影響とヒト-ヒト感染拡大の懸念があり、IHR基準複数該当。
triage.notes: WHOが過去最大規模と認定した流行であり、複数国際機関（Africa CDC, WHO, Oxford大学, ロシア）が関与。フルRRAへの移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: 중국, 또 '코로나' 유행하나...양성률 20%에 ''일반적 수준'' 해명
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China, another 'coronavirus' outbreak? Officials say a 20% positivity rate is a 'normal level'.
article.articleSummary: China reports a rebound of COVID-19, with the national positivity rate rising to 20.3% in the fourth week of last month among respiratory samples from outpatient and emergency department patients with influenza-like illness, meaning about one in five tests were positive for SARS-CoV-2. The Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention characterizes the surge as mid-level and within normal seasonal fluctuations, similar to trends over the past two years. Most infections are mild, but elderly individuals and those with chronic conditions remain at risk for progression to severe disease. The NB.1.8.1 variant lineage is currently dominant. Regional data show higher positivity in southern China than in the north, and higher rates among the 15–59 age group. Published 2026-08-02.

triage.headline_ja: 中国、再び「コロナ」流行か…陽性率20%に「通常レベル」と説明
triage.triage_reason: 中国当局は季節的変動の範囲内と説明しており、重症例急増や異常性の明確な根拠はないが、陽性率20%という数値と新変異株の動向は継続的な監視が必要。
triage.notes: 中国CDCは季節的な範囲内の中程度の流行と説明。重症化は高齢者・基礎疾患保有者に限定的で、新変異株NB.1.8.1が優勢との報告あり。

article.articleHeadline: 흘러간 물 코로나19 中에서 다시 꿈틀
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Water That Has Flowed Stirs Again Amid COVID-19
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is increasing again in China, with a 20.3% positivity rate for SARS-CoV-2 among influenza-like illness visits to outpatient and emergency departments during the 20–26th of the last month. No deaths have been reported, and officials characterize the trend as a mid-level, cyclical pattern similar to prior years. The NB.1.8.1 lineage is the dominant circulating variant, with higher positivity in southern China than northern regions. Among age groups, 15–59-year-olds show notably higher positivity. Most infections are mild; however, elderly individuals and those with chronic diseases remain at risk of severe disease. The report notes ongoing respiratory pathogen activity but does not indicate a severe outbreak or mortality, suggesting continued vigilance without a fatal escalation.

triage.headline_ja: 流れ去った水、COVID-19が中国で再び蠢く
triage.triage_reason: 中国でCOVID-19陽性率が上昇しているが、例年と同様の中程度・周期的パターンで死亡例もなく、現時点では重大な公衆衛生上の脅威とは言えないため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: COVID-19の季節的・周期的な増加であり、例年同様のパターンとされ、死亡例なし。高齢者や基礎疾患患者は重症化リスクがあるため、今後の動向を監視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Nůžky se rozevírají. Kongo čelí masivnímu šíření eboly, Uganda hlásí úspěšné zvládnutí nákazy
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Scissors Are Opening. Congo Faces a Massive Spread of Ebola, Uganda Reports Successful Containment of the Outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Massive Ebola spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while Uganda reports containment. The DRC outbreak has killed more than 1,500 people; Uganda cites about two dozen infections and says the outbreak is under control after the last patient was discharged. Ugandan authorities credit prior outbreak experience, crisis planning, and rapid setup of a specialized center in Kampala within a day after first cases. Strict preventive measures and public cooperation were pivotal: more than 6,000 contacts were traced and placed in 21-day quarantine, and borders with Congo were temporarily closed to prevent cross-border spread. The DRC faces harsher conditions: delayed detection of a rare Ebola lineage and insecurity in the east with armed rebel groups, causing mass displacement and hampering case finding. Uganda warns risk persists along the long border; it has dispatched health workers into Congo to help quell the outbreak there, noting victory requires stabilization in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: はさみが開いていく。コンゴは大規模なエボラ感染拡大に直面、ウガンダは感染制圧に成功と報告
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラにより1500人超が死亡する大規模流行が続いており、稀な系統株や治安悪化により対応が困難化。国境封鎖等の措置も取られており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダも記事の主題に含まれるが対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めない。DRCでの流行が本記事の主要な懸念点。

article.articleHeadline: 重要！河南疾控最新提示_手机网易网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Important! Henan Center for Disease Control and Prevention's Latest Advisory - NetEase Mobile
article.articleSummary: Henan Province’s Center for Disease Control and Prevention issued August risk guidance. With alternating high temperatures and heavy rains, humid conditions foster vectors and pathogens, while holiday travel raises exposure to vector-borne diseases and foodborne risks. Vector-borne diseases to watch include dengue fever, chikungunya fever, fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and malaria; prevention includes environmental management (eliminate standing water, seal containers, install screens) and personal protection (long sleeves, repellents, avoid peak mosquito times), and monitoring travel history to prevent imported cases. For food poisoning, the high-temperature, high-humidity season (May–October) increases microbial growth and toxins; ensure licensing checks, proper storage and hygiene, cook thoroughly, and seek care if symptoms occur. Extreme weather—heat waves, heavy rainfall, thunderstorms—requires heat prevention and flood safety with vigilance for warnings. Summer holidays demand reinforced supervision to prevent drowning, road, burn, and other injuries.

triage.headline_ja: 重要！河南省疾病予防管理センターの最新注意喚起
triage.triage_reason: 季節性の一般的な予防啓発情報であり、具体的な患者発生や異常な流行状況の報告がないため、シグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: 本記事は具体的な症例数や発生状況を報告するものではなく、河南省疾控中心による夏季の一般的な感染症・食中毒・熱中症等への注意喚起（季節性ガイダンス）である。特定の異常発生や流行拡大の兆候は記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Nuova ondata di Covid in Cina in piena estate, registrato un picco di casi con la variante NB.1.8.1
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New wave of COVID in China in midsummer, recording a peak in cases with the NB.1.8.1 variant.
article.articleSummary: China records a summer 2026 COVID surge driven by the Omicron NB.1.8.1 subvariant, with test positivity rising to 20.3%. In July, about 79,000 infections were logged, including 130 severe cases, with higher incidence in southern provinces. Sentinel hospital surveillance shows SARS-CoV-2 as the leading respiratory pathogen, overtaking influenza. The NB.1.8.1 lineage is classified by WHO as a variant under monitoring since May 2025; analyses from the Chinese CDC and international networks note greater transmissibility and partial immune evasion but no increase in virulence or clinical severity. Most patients exhibit fever, cough, and sore throat with a 5–7 day course. Europe is not alarmed due to vaccination coverage and available care. Virologists Fabrizio Pregliasco and Matteo Bassetti emphasize vigilance for the elderly, immunocompromised, and those with chronic diseases, despite the generally milder impact on the broader population.

triage.headline_ja: 中国で真夏に新型コロナの新たな波、変異株NB.1.8.1で感染ピークを記録
triage.triage_reason: 中国でCOVID-19感染者が季節的に増加しているが、WHOは既に本変異株を監視下に置いており、重症度の増加は認められていないため、緊急のフルRRAは不要だが動向は注視すべき。
triage.notes: NB.1.8.1はWHOが2025年5月から監視下に置く変異株で、伝播性増加・免疫回避の可能性はあるが重症度増加の報告はない。欧州は現時点で警戒レベルを引き上げていない。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Avian Influenza A H5N1

article.articleHeadline: Kiểm soát chặt chẽ, không chủ quan với dịch cúm gia cầm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Strict control, no room for complacency with avian influenza
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza A(H5N1) outbreaks persist in Vietnam, with Hà Tĩnh province reporting a local cluster in Cam Duệ commune. Since July 13, 2026, 228 poultry across five households were infected; 120 chickens from one family were culled, and barns disinfected. Authorities vaccinated more than 15,600 birds across three hamlets (Quốc Tiến, Na Trung, Trần Phú), posted warning signs, and applied lime powder and disinfectants in containment zones. Nationwide, Vietnam has recorded 80 outbreaks in 73 communes across 17 provinces, with more than 349,400 poultry dying or being culled. Nghệ An, a neighboring province, shows rising outbreak activity. Hà Tĩnh reports a large total poultry stock (~10 million) and challenges including low first-round vaccination coverage and incomplete disease reporting on some farms. Officials urge intensified surveillance, supplementary H5N1 vaccination, biosafety, reporting, and strict monitoring of live poultry markets to prevent year-end spread.

triage.headline_ja: 鳥インフルエンザに対する厳格な管理、油断は禁物
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム国内で家禽のH5N1感染が広範囲に継続しているが、記事はヒト感染例を報告しておらず、公衆衛生への直接的な深刻性は現時点で不明であるため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 疾患名はヒトのH5N1感染症とされているが、記事内容は家禽（鳥）における発生に限定されており、人への感染報告は確認されていない。ベトナム全国で80件の発生、17省に拡大しており、家禽業界への影響は継続的かつ広範。

article.articleHeadline: 中国冠病阳性率突破20% 中疾控强调属常规周期波动 - 国际 - 即时国际
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 positivity rate surpasses 20%; China CDC emphasizes that it is a normal cyclical fluctuation - International - Real-Time International
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 positivity among sentinel hospital respiratory samples in China rose to 20.3% during July 20–26, 2026, up from 16.3% a week earlier, per the China CDC. The rise indicates a moderate cyclical fluctuation with no major impact on overall medical order. The dominant lineage remains NB.1.8.1. Positivity is higher in southern provinces than in northern regions, with the 15–59 age group showing the highest positivity. Since shifting to Category B management, COVID-19 has become a common, recurring respiratory infection with 1–2 waves per year; the increase mirrors patterns of the past two years. Severity remains largely mild, though the elderly and those with chronic diseases stay at higher risk for severe disease, and existing specific antiviral therapies remain effective. No variants detected with major public health risk.

triage.headline_ja: 中国のCOVID-19陽性率が20%を突破、中国疾病予防管理センターは通常の周期的変動と強調
triage.triage_reason: 中国CDCが季節的・周期的な変動と説明しており、重症度は軽度、公衆衛生上の重大リスクを持つ変異株も検出されていないため、シグナルとして扱う必要性は低い。
triage.notes: 既知の変異株NB.1.8.1による季節的増加であり、過去2年間のパターンと一致。特段の異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: 中国新冠感染率破20% 南方省份患者高于北方 | 中國報 China Press
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 infection rate exceeds 20%; patients in southern provinces have higher infection rates than those in northern provinces.
article.articleSummary: China CDC's latest respiratory infection surveillance shows a continued rise in SARS-CoV-2 positivity. For July 20-26, 2026, the detection positivity rate for COVID-19 surpassed 20% — the first time — up 4 percentage points from the prior week and higher than influenza at 14.5%. The data come from the National Acute Respiratory Infections Sentinel Surveillance Situation (Week 30), published July 30. The report notes regional differences, with Southern provinces reporting higher infection rates than Northern provinces. No case counts or deaths are provided in the brief. The trend indicates ongoing community transmission of SARS-CoV-2 during late July 2026 in China, with COVID-19 leading respiratory pathogen activity within the surveillance window.

triage.headline_ja: 中国新型コロナ感染率が20%突破、南方省の患者数が北方より多い
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19陽性率上昇を示す定期サーベイランスデータだが、症例数・死亡者数等の重症度情報がなく、既知の季節的流行パターンの範囲内とも考えられるため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 中国CDCの定期呼吸器感染症サーベイランス（第30週）に基づく報告。症例数・死亡者数のデータなし。COVID-19は既に流行病として定着しており、季節的な陽性率変動の可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية تشهد أسرع انتشار لفيروس "إيبولا" في تاريخها
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is witnessing the fastest spread of the Ebola virus in its history.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing the fastest Ebola spread in its history, according to Africa CDC. Uganda declared its outbreak over on July 28, while the DRC has recorded 3,605 cases and 1,587 deaths to date. In the week of July 21–27, 2026, 488 new infections were reported, up about 50%. The Podibojio lineage has driven rising positivity, from 37.8% to 46.9% in a month, complicating containment and contact tracing. Africa CDC notes more than 130,000 contacts should be followed based on confirmed cases, but only around 13,000 are being monitored. Over 80% of new infections are not linked to known chains, further hindering response. Hospital bed occupancy averages 80%, with severe crowding in North Kivu. The ChaDoX1 candidate vaccine is undergoing testing.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、史上最速のエボラ拡大に直面
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最速のエボラ拡大が発生し、死亡者多数・接触者追跡の破綻・病床逼迫など公衆衛生上深刻な影響があり、IHR基準複数該当およびWPRO基準も複数該当するためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダは既にアウトブレイク終息を宣言済みのため対象国リストに含まれない（またWPRO対象国リストにも含まれていない）。DRCのみが現在進行中の主題国。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in DR Congo Out of Control: WHO Warns of Rising Risk
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control, with the epidemiological situation deteriorating and cross-border transmission risk rising. As of July 30, 2026, 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths have been reported, yielding a crude case fatality ratio of 44%. The outbreak is the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the DR Congo, with expanding geographic spread and persistently high mortality. In the most recent complete reporting week (epidemiological week 30), 567 cases and 296 deaths were recorded—the highest weekly totals to date, underscoring exceptional transmission speed. Insecurity, population displacement and mobility, and cross-border movements complicate response efforts and increase the risk of further regional spread. Geneva, August 2, 2026. WHO warns the outbreak remains out of control and that cross-border transmission to neighboring countries is increasingly likely.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、制御不能に:WHOがリスク増大を警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行が制御不能な状態にあり、致死率44%と高く、越境拡大リスクをWHOが警告しているためIHR基準複数該当。
triage.notes: Genève/Switzerlandの地域情報はWHO本部所在地であり発生地域ではないため除外。DRCが史上最大規模のエボラ流行で、週次症例数・死亡数とも過去最高を更新中。

article.articleHeadline: Mumbai Monsoon Health Tips: बारिश के मौसम में बीमारी से बचना है तो अभी अपनाएं ये आसान उपाय! डेंगू, मलेरिया और वायरल फीवर से बचाव के लिए जानें असरदार घरेलू नुस्खे
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mumbai Monsoon Health Tips: To avoid illness during the rainy season, adopt these simple remedies now! Learn effective home remedies to prevent dengue, malaria, and viral fever.
article.articleSummary: On August 2, 2026, Mumbai faces elevated monsoon risks from dengue, malaria, chikungunya, leptospirosis, and viral fever (typhoid and food poisoning also noted). Prevent mosquito breeding by eliminating standing water from homes, balconies, and rooftops; clean coolers, pots, and water tanks weekly; use nets or repellents in morning and evening; wear long sleeves; and ensure regular fogging and cleaning around the home. Guard against water- and foodborne illness by drinking boiled or filtered water, avoiding open or stale foods, eating freshly prepared meals, and washing hands. After rain, dry clothes promptly; wear boots in dirty water. Home remedies like tulsi tea, ginger, black pepper tea, turmeric milk, and limited giloy/amla, plus vitamin C fruits and ORS, may help immunity. Seek medical care for fever ≥102°F, vomiting, severe pain, breathing difficulty, rashes, bleeding, or fainting. Papaya leaf juice is not a proven dengue cure.

article.articleHeadline: World News | WHO: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Spiralling out of Control, Risk of Transmission Escalating
article.articleSummary: WHO says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spiralling out of control. As of 30 July 2026, 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths have been reported, a crude case fatality ratio of 44%, making it the largest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo's history. The situation is deteriorating with the highest weekly transmission to date in epidemiological week 30, recording 567 new cases and 296 deaths. Ongoing transmission is exacerbated by insecurity, population displacement, mobility, and cross-border movements, complicating response operations and raising the risk of spread to neighbouring countries. The report underscores rapidly evolving emergency dynamics and the urgent need for intensified surveillance, containment, and international support to avert further geographical spread.

article.articleHeadline: Kerala sees HIV surge among men in their 20s | Part 1
article.articleSummary: Kerala reports rising HIV infections among youths, driven by men who have sex with men (MSM). In 2025-2026, MSM accounted for 29% of new HIV-positive individuals enrolled at Care and Support Centres (CSCs); in the first quarter of the current financial year, 31% were MSM. The 15–24 age group rose from 9% of new infections in 2022 to 14.2% in 2024, and 15.4% between April–October 2025. District data show: Kasaragod—52 new cases in 2025-2026, with seven of the first three months’ 10 cases MSM (two were students); Palakkad—120 new cases, 38 MSM; Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram—426 new cases, 155 MSM, of whom 115 were 24 or younger; Ernakulam and Thrissur—417 new cases at Thrissur CSC, 116 MSM, 29 injection drug users. Counsellors note underreporting due to anonymity; many MSM meet partners online and struggle to disclose contacts. Emphasis remains on safe sex, status awareness, and ART/Ushas access.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: The Ebola outbreak in Congo, the largest of its kind ever.
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization says the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the largest on record, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak that had 3,317 confirmed cases. As of last Thursday, 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths have been reported, a case fatality rate of 44%. The past epidemiologic week (week 30) recorded the highest weekly burden to date with 567 new cases and 296 deaths, underscoring accelerated transmission. The outbreak has spread across five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Uele, and Tshopo—now affecting 49 health zones. Authorities, with WHO and partners, continue wide‑scale response measures. WHO stresses sustained surveillance, monitoring, and preparedness given ongoing population movement and rising risk of cross‑border transmission.

article.articleSummary: Largest Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 3,605 laboratory-confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths reported as of last Thursday. In the past week, the highest weekly totals were 567 cases and 296 deaths, underscoring exceptionally rapid transmission. The outbreak has spread to five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Uele, and Tshopo—affecting 49 health zones. Ebola spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids and causes severe fever and hemorrhagic symptoms. Historically, Ebola outbreaks in Africa have resulted in more than 15,000 deaths over five decades. The report highlights ongoing geographic expansion and the urgent need for intensified public health response.

article.articleHeadline: 🐚 Laos pushes back parasitic disease to below one percent
article.articleSummary: Schistosomiasis in Laos has fallen to under 1% prevalence in the worst-affected areas, down from over 40% in 2003, with Champasack Province remaining the last transmission focus and about 120,000 people in 202 villages at risk. In 2024, over 95,000 individuals received a yearly single-dose treatment that clears the parasite and halts transmission. The snail-borne disease, spread by freshwater snails in water used for washing, fishing, and transport along the Mekong River, can cause enlarged liver and bleeding during toileting, with severe cases leading to fatal liver damage. The program combines mass treatment, water/sanitation improvements, and health education, with strengthened surveillance by China’s NIPD and the Swiss Tropical/Public Health Institute. Cross-border collaboration with Cambodia and support from WHO, China, and Switzerland totaling about $1.18 million underpins progress. Malaria fell to 272 cases in 2025.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cities in the Interior of São Paulo Begin Measles Vaccination Campaign on August 3
article.articleSummary: Measles vaccination campaign launches Aug 3 in interior municipalities of São Paulo, Brazil, prompted by a spike of measles cases in the state capital. The multivaccination operation runs through Sep 1 across all state health units, focusing on updating vaccine records for children and youths up to 15 years old and delivering measles vaccine plus other vaccines on the official schedule (polio and hepatitis). Authorities aim to extend preventive actions to rural areas and small towns, with active case finding in schools and community settings to locate unvaccinated children amid high transmissibility and risk of pneumonia and encephalitis. The campaign, integrated by municipal secretariats and health centers, reinforces epidemiological surveillance and ensures routine immunizations are up to date, reducing gaps and preventing future outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: How Virunga Park protects people and gorillas from Ebola in eastern DRC
article.articleSummary: Ebola continues to spread across eastern DRC and Uganda, prompting Virunga National Park to mount a proactive health response as of 2 August 2026. The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May. Virunga set up six health checkpoints along its 300-km North Kivu corridor, deploying 40 paramedics and 80 rangers for an initial six-month emergency response. Each checkpoint includes handwashing facilities, temperature screening, and isolation space, with two suspected cases identified and referred to public health authorities. The response builds on lessons from 2018–2020, when nearly 2,300 died in North Kivu and Ituri. The current outbreak has killed more than 1,400, with Ituri as the epicenter. Gorillas—fewer than 1,100 in the Greater Virunga Landscape—face spillover risk, though no mountain gorilla has contracted Ebola to date; monitoring and visitor screening aim to prevent human-to-animal transmission.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Danger of Lime Dust Pollution in West Bandung: Hundreds of Residents Suspected of TB and Infected with Severe Acute Respiratory Infection.
article.articleSummary: Lime limestone dust pollution in West Bandung (Padalarang and Cipatat, Bandung Barat) is linked to respiratory illness among residents. Between July 25–31, 2026, health authorities screened 2,870 people (out of 2,974 visits) under a Free Health Check program across four Puskesmas: Sumurbandung, Jayamekar, Tagogapu, and Cipatat. Of those screened, 1,772 (61.7%) had chest X-rays. Results show 378 people as suspected tuberculosis (TB) and 267 with Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI); 304 TB suspects underwent Molecular Rapid Testing (TCM) to confirm TB. Additionally, 25 residents were suspected of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). A notable risk factor identified is 549 smokers among the tested group. The findings indicate limestone dust exposure may drive respiratory disease, prompting ongoing surveillance, screening, and diagnostic follow-up.

article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak in Brazil prompts an expanded vaccination campaign in São Paulo state. The Ministry of Health alerted São Paulo city, Guarulhos, and São Bernardo do Campo after 15 of 18 confirmed measles cases in Brazil in 2026 were concentrated there. The campaign runs August 3 to September 1 and targets residents and workers aged 6 months to 59 years in the three municipalities, regardless of prior MMR vaccination. A supplementary vaccine dose is offered; proof of prior doses is not required. In São Paulo city, 12 cases; São Bernardo do Campo, two; Guarulhos, one. Two patients in the capital had traveled to Bolivia and Guatemala; others were infected domestically. The outbreak is active; São Paulo is the only state with confirmed infections. A 6–11 month dose zero is available for partial protection; measles can cause pneumonia, encephalitis, diarrhea, and otitis, with higher risk in young children and the immunocompromised.

article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in China shows rising positivity, surpassing 20% in the week of 20–26 last month. Most infections are mild; however, risk of progression to severe disease exists for older adults and those with chronic conditions. The dominant lineage among cases is NB.1.8.1. Regional distribution shows higher positivity in southern China than in the north; ages 15–59 have higher positivity. The report emphasizes continued surveillance and caution for vulnerable populations despite overall mild presentations.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo worsens, with more than 3,500 confirmed cases—the second-largest in history.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-02, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 3,500 confirmed cases, the second-largest on record. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain. WHO notes the epicenters are in areas of ongoing armed conflict and dense population movement; treatment centers are near capacity, and security concerns hinder surveillance, isolation, and contact tracing. No proven effective vaccine or specific antiviral therapy exists yet. WHO is coordinating international collaboration, including candidate vaccines and novel therapies in clinical trials, to accelerate control. Given ongoing safety and displacement crises, cross-border cooperation is crucial, as the outbreak risks spreading to neighboring countries without improvements in security and public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Current Ebola outbreak largest ever recorded in DR Congo: WHO
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, is the largest on record, with 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality rate 44%), according to the WHO. It surpasses the 2018–2020 eastern outbreak, which had 3,317 cases. Originating in Mongbwalu health zone, Ituri province, the outbreak has spread over two months to 49 health zones across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo. Health workers have suffered 151 infections and 44 deaths. Insecurity, population displacement, high mobility and cross-border movements are hampering surveillance and response. Access to healthcare, clean water, food and shelter is limited in conflict-affected areas, and attacks on health facilities hinder response and can increase transmission. WHO assesses the national risk as very high and urges expanded surveillance, testing, clinical care, infection control, community engagement and logistics to curb spread.

article.articleHeadline: Centre steps up dengue surveillance as monsoon raises outbreak risk | Today News
article.articleSummary: Dengue surveillance in India is being intensified as the monsoon season creates favorable Aedes breeding conditions and potential El Niño-driven transmission risks. The health ministry has urged states to tighten dengue surveillance, expand laboratory testing with ELISA-based NS1 (first five days) and IgM kits, and boost larval source management with digital reporting via the IHIP-VBD portal. Hospitals should prepare contingency plans and rapid-response teams; ensure laboratories and insecticide stocks are functional. So far this year, 13,336 dengue cases and 12 deaths have been reported. Historically, India logged 121,824 cases and 131 deaths in 2025; 233,519/297 in 2024; and 289,235/485 in 2023. Tamil Nadu leads with 4,973 cases and 2 deaths; Maharashtra 1,525; Kerala 1,403 (10 deaths); Karnataka 978; Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal 770 each. Takeda’s dengue vaccine has been approved in India, expected next year, amid broader vector-borne disease mitigation including chikungunya and Zika.

article.articleSummary: Cyclosporiasis outbreaks exceed 20,000 cases, with the total likely higher; CDC to update patient counts next week, and the source of the largest outbreak remains unidentified. UK Health Security Agency notes increasing Cyclospora infections among travelers returning from Mexico, predicting additional travel-associated cases tied to summer visits to Mexico and the United States. Ineos Oxford Institute links the global spread of Campylobacter to industrial chicken farming, noting wild-bird–origin strains entering poultry flocks and rising antibiotic resistance. In South Korea, a study on raw fish consumption shows Kudoa septempunctata transmission from farmed olive flounder may be slowing after COVID-19-era dining restrictions. China reports mushroom poisonings reaching a six-year high in 2025, though fatalities were the lowest in that period. article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: Democratic Republic of the Congo Faces Its Largest Ebola Outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the largest on record. The World Health Organization reported 3,605 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases and 1,587 deaths as of last Thursday, with 567 new cases and 296 deaths in the past week—the highest weekly totals to date. The outbreak has expanded geographically into five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Uele and Tshopo—and now affects 49 health zones. Local authorities, WHO, and partners are implementing wide-ranging response measures, but officials say significant scaling up of response activities is required to advance containment. Ebola virus disease spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever. Over the past 50 years in Africa, the Ebola virus has killed more than 15,000 people. The report underscores ongoing transmission and the urgent need for intensified interventions.

article.articleHeadline: Sưng mang tai, người đàn ông 60 tuổi nguy kịch vì vi khuẩn ăn thịt người
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ear swelling, a 60-year-old man in critical condition due to necrotizing fasciitis
article.articleSummary: A 60-year-old man admitted to Phu Tho General Hospital in Vietnam with progressive swelling around the right ear due to a salivary-gland abscess and fever. About a week earlier a small lump appeared; self-medication failed to help, and swelling increased. Clinicians diagnosed spreading cellulitis with an abscess; surgical drainage was performed and pus cultured. Culture identified Burkholderia pseudomallei, the agent of Whitmore disease (melioidosis). He was transferred to the Tropical Diseases Ward and started on antibiotics per susceptibility testing, with supportive care. Fever resolved and the abscess reduced markedly, with good response to therapy. Melioidosis is a dangerous infection that can cause bacteremia and multi‑organ damage, with high mortality if not diagnosed and treated. The bacterium is endemic in tropical regions, especially Southeast Asia and northern Australia, acquired via skin breaks or inhalation. Early lab confirmation and targeted antibiotics improve outcomes.

article.articleHeadline: Viaggi e vacanze, attenzione a chikungunya e dengue: i consigli per chi va nelle aree a rischio
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Travel and holidays: beware chikungunya and dengue — tips for those going to risk areas
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya and dengue are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, with rising travel-related risk. Globally, chikungunya is reported in over 110 countries, with confirmed transmission in more than 50 in the last five years; dengue circulates across Africa, Southeast Asia, India, the Middle East, the Americas and Australia. Italy has seen local chikungunya foci in Veneto and Emilia-Romagna (last year) and autochthonous dengue in Lodi (2023) and Fano (2024). Chikungunya symptoms appear 3–7 days after a bite: fever, rash, fatigue and severe joint pain; chronic arthritis can follow; rare organ involvement. Dengue is often milder, but secondary infection with a different serotype can cause severe dengue; no specific cure exists for either. Prevention relies on repellents, long sleeves, light clothing, bed nets and daytime insecticides, since Aedes bites at dawn and dusk. Vaccines: chikungunya vaccine available in Italy since Oct 2025 for 12+, single dose 14 days before travel; dengue vaccine, for 4+, is two doses 3 months apart, no serology required, with strongest benefit for those previously infected. SIMVIM recommends vaccination for travelers to endemic areas, especially older adults, those with chronic disease, and pregnant women who cannot delay travel. Climate change and vector behavior may raise cases in Italy; inform travelers and maintain prevention.

triage.headline_ja: 旅行と休暇：チクングニア熱とデング熱に注意 — リスク地域へ行く人へのアドバイス
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は旅行医学的な一般的注意喚起・予防接種案内であり、特定国での新規アウトブレイクや異常事態を報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はイタリア国内での過去の局地的発生（Veneto、Emilia-Romagna、Lodi、Fano）とワクチン接種推奨に関する一般的旅行医学情報。インドは流行地域の一例として言及されているのみで、具体的なアウトブレイクイベントの発生地ではないため対象国として計上しない。イタリアは対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: South Africa hopeful of possible TB vaccine breakthrough
article.articleSummary: South Africa is preparing for potential rollout of the M27 tuberculosis vaccine, aiming to align registration and introduction promptly if ongoing trials demonstrate safety and efficacy. The department targets TB elimination as a public health threat by 2030, with M27 already showing promise in Phase I/II and currently in Phase III trials in South Africa, Kenya, Zambia, Malawi, and Indonesia. If SAHPRA approves the vaccine, it would mark the first new TB vaccine in more than a century, offering protection for adolescents and adults. Early preparations seek to prevent delays in vaccine access for communities. Global partners, including the Gates Medical Research Institute and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, have an agreement with the Serum Institute of India to manufacture and supply doses worldwide, potentially enabling local manufacturing partnerships in South Africa and Indonesia.

triage.headline_ja: 南アフリカ、結核ワクチンの実用化に期待
triage.triage_reason: 既知の疾病（結核）に対するワクチン開発の進捗報告であり、異常な公衆衛生事象や急性のアウトブレイクではないため、トリアージ対象外と判断。
triage.notes: 記事はTBワクチン（M27）の第III相試験進捗とワクチン導入準備に関する内容であり、疾病アウトブレイクの報告ではない。南アフリカ・ケニア・マラウイは対象国リスト外のため除外。インドはワクチン製造提携の文脈のみで発生国ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en Ituri : les résistances des voyageurs compliquent le contrôle sanitaire - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Ituri: travellers' resistance complicates health screening - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak response teams in Ituri Province, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, report resistance from travellers at health screening points, complicating preventive measures. Some motorcycle taxi drivers and their passengers refuse to alight or to participate in handwashing, temperature checks, and other surveillance steps, though controls are intended to protect individuals, families, and the community from Ebola spread. Dr Théophile Ponde, provincial coordinator of the National Border Hygiene Program (PNHF), emphasizes education and states that precautions are protective rather than punitive. Response efforts prioritize sensitization and accompaniment while ensuring adherence to the established screening circuit. The operation involves surveillance pillar teams, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), and risk communication units to reduce hesitancy as Ebola response remains active in northeastern Ituri. No case or death counts are cited in the article.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州でのエボラ出血熱：旅行者の抵抗が保健検疫を複雑化させる - ACP
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱はIHR基準における重大・異常な公衆衛生事象であり、DRCイツリ州で対応が継続中であることから、症例数不明でもフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事は症例数・死亡者数を報告しておらず、検疫活動における住民の抵抗に焦点を当てている。エボラという疾患特性上、既存のアウトブレイク対応の一環として継続監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 中國COVID-19感染率升破20％
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 infection rate surpasses 20%
article.articleSummary: China’s COVID-19 test-positivity rate surpassed 20% in Week 30 of 2026 (July 20–26) per the Chinese CDC’s national sentinel surveillance, marking the first time the weekly positivity exceeded 20%. The overall positivity rose by 4 percentage points from the prior week, equating to about one in five individuals testing positive. Southern provinces show higher positivity than northern regions. Age groups most affected are children 0–4 years, adults 15–59 years, and seniors 60+ years. Officials characterize the rise as a periodic fluctuation with intensity similar to the past two years, with no evidence of a more severe illness pattern or a major new variant. No significant public health risk has been identified, though ongoing monitoring of acute respiratory infections and SARS-CoV-2 activity continues. Date reference based on 2026-08-02 publication.

triage.headline_ja: 中国のCOVID-19感染率が20%を突破
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19陽性率の季節的上昇であり、当局は過去数年と同程度の周期的変動で新たな重症化パターンや変異株の証拠はないとしており、公衆衛生上の重大リスクは認められていない。
triage.notes: 中国CDCのサーベイランスデータに基づく定例報告であり、当局は重大なリスクはないと評価している。

article.articleHeadline: Des caméras thermiques installées pour renforcer la surveillance d'Ebola à l'aéroport de Bunia - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Thermal cameras installed to strengthen Ebola surveillance at Bunia Airport - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Thermal cameras installed at Murongo Airport in Bunia, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, aim to strengthen Ebola surveillance among travelers. The move, announced by Dr. Théophile Ponde, coordinator of the National Border Health Program (PNHF), adds to existing health measures including hand sanitizer dispensers and a digital traveler registration system using QR codes. The cameras screen for fever, one of the earliest Ebola symptoms, enabling rapid, non-contact detection and isolation of travelers with elevated temperatures. Data digitalization and QR-based recording are designed to improve entry-point surveillance and pre-empt local transmission. Travelers departing Bunia must pass through the registration system. The measures illustrate ongoing border health reinforcement against Ebola in an area already alert to potential outbreaks, with emphasis on early detection at air travel hubs.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、ブニア空港でエボラ出血熱監視強化のためサーモカメラを設置
triage.triage_reason: エボラ監視体制強化に関する記事であり、新規感染や患者発生の具体的報告はないが、DRCにおけるエボラリスクへの継続的警戒を示すため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事は空港での体温スクリーニング等の予防的監視強化措置についてであり、新規症例や具体的な発生状況の報告はない。DRC当局がエボラ再燃を警戒している背景がうかがえるが、続報の有無を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola au Haut-Uele : l'équipe de la riposte renforcée par trois ambulances tout terrain - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Haut-Uele: the response team reinforced by three all-terrain ambulances - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Haut-Uele, northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, sees reinforced response with three all-terrain ambulances and a batch of medicines donated by the central government to Isiro. Governor Jean Bakomito says the assets bolster the response across five health zones (including Wamba, Boma-Mangbetu, Pawa, Isiro, and Rungu) out of Haut-Uele’s 13 zones, building on two ambulances already acquired by the provincial government and an additional vehicle for Wamba. The ceremony at the provincial governorate esplanade, Isiro, was attended by Vice-Governor Christophe Dara Matata and health officials. Dr. Patrick Banza, provincial health chief, called the logistics a major asset for rapid Ebola case management and surveillance. The governor urged responsible use and veteran collaboration with the central government to stop transmission and strengthen the province’s health system, while Justin Zamba Ndezu urged community adherence to prevention measures."}{

triage.headline_ja: オー・ウエレ州のエボラ出血熱：対応チームが全地形対応救急車3台で強化 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国オー・ウエレ州でエボラ出血熱の対応が継続中であり、複数の保健地区に影響が及んでいる。エボラは重篤性・異常性・国際拡大リスクが高く、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は既存のエボラ対応強化に関する内容であり、新規発生の詳細（症例数・死亡者数等）は記載されていないが、エボラという疾患特性上、フルRRAへの引き上げが妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola dans la Tshopo : une mission conjointe renforce la vigilance à Bafwasende - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Tshopo Province: a joint mission heightens vigilance in Bafwasende - ACP
article.articleSummary: Seven Ebola cases in DRC's Tshopo Province are imported from Ituri, with both patients and corpses crossing the Avakubi barrier in Bafwasende, near Kisangani. A joint mission by the provincial health and interior ministries and the World Health Organization visited Bafwasende to strengthen the Ebola response and to disseminate governor's decrees prohibiting entry of corpses from Ebola-affected zones. Authorities stressed strict health measures, including temperature screening, handwashing, and traveler checks, noting some individuals refuse compliance. The effort aims to protect the Tshopo border with Ituri, the outbreak epicenter, and urged border posts, local authorities, and communities to boost communication and vigilance to prevent further spread. Dr. Simon Bokongo, provincial health minister, warned of Ebola's severe, highly contagious nature and called for broad community involvement due to potential humanitarian and economic consequences if the disease spreads in Tshopo.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国ツショポ州のエボラ:合同ミッションがバフワセンデでの警戒を強化
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がイトゥリ州からツショポ州へ越境拡大しており、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクがあるためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: イトゥリ州が発生源(epicenter)であり、症例と遺体がバフワセンデ経由でツショポ州へ越境していることが確認されている。WHOも合同対応に参加している。

article.articleHeadline: Congo : l'épidémie d'Ebola s'intensifie à un rythme "exceptionnel", avertit l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: the Ebola outbreak is intensifying at an exceptional rate, warns the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is intensifying at an exceptional rate, the World Health Organization (WHO) warns. The current outbreak is the largest ever recorded in the DRC, surpassing the 2018–2020 epidemic. As of last Thursday, 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths have been reported. The most recent week recorded a record 567 new cases and 296 deaths, confirming ongoing rapid transmission. The outbreak is expanding geographically into five provinces, signaling broader spread. WHO urges a major scale-up of the public health response to contain transmission and avert further fatalities. The figures come from the WHO’s latest report published on the X platform; the article provides case and death counts without detailing symptoms or infection sources.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ：エボラ出血熱の流行が「異例の」速さで拡大、WHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで過去最大規模に拡大し、致死率も高く、5州へ地理的拡大している。IHR基準複数該当かつ国際的関心が高い。
triage.notes: WHOが公衆衛生対応の大幅な強化を要請しており、致死率(約44%)が高い。過去最大規模のエボラ流行で国際的な注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: RDC: epidemia de Ebola intensifica-se a um ritmo "excepcional", alerta a OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Ebola epidemic intensifies at an 'exceptional' pace, WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: As of August 2, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality rate 44%), according to WHO. There is currently no vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo strain. This Bundibugyo-strain epidemic, declared May 15, is the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the DRC and is intensifying with high transmission. It has spread from Ituri to Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces, with ongoing infections among healthcare workers (151 cases, 44 deaths). Authorities and WHO are implementing large-scale response measures, but substantial scale-up is needed to anticipate the epidemic. In Uganda, authorities say the Ebola outbreak ended, yet WHO notes residual risk. Vaccine development progresses: Hilleman Laboratories (Singapore) will develop a vaccine, described by WHO as the most promising; separately, Oxford University (UK) has a Bundibugyo-targeting vaccine in a first-in-human trial.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:エボラ流行が「異例」のペースで激化、WHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行(3,605例、死亡1,587例、致死率44%)が急速に拡大し複数州に広がり、医療従事者にも感染が発生しているためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当。
triage.notes: ウガンダは流行終息が報告されているが残存リスクがWHOにより指摘されている。シンガポール・英国はワクチン開発拠点であり発生地域ではないためverified_locationsに含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Cuiabá intensifica monitoramento de zoonoses e mantém vigilância ativa para proteger a população
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cuiabá Intensifies Monitoring of Zoonotic Diseases and Maintains Active Surveillance to Protect the Population
article.articleSummary: Cuiabá's Municipal Health Secretariat (SMS) maintains environmental and epidemiological surveillance to monitor zoonoses. In the first half of 2026, 88 epizootic notifications were recorded, focused on primates and wild birds as sentinels for yellow fever and avian influenza. Visceral leishmaniasis was the most frequent canine disease, with 782 inspections and 249 confirmed canine cases; one human case was confirmed. Sporotrichosis appeared in cats (21 notifications, 17 lab-confirmed); 13 human suspects with 6 confirmations. Rabies surveillance remained intense: 62 notifications of dead or neurologically affected animals, 6 veterinary visits for suspicious behavior, and 52 companion animals with bat contact. The human side recorded 753 anti-rabies consultations, 125 severe cases. Yellow fever epizootics in 14 monkeys were suspected but none confirmed. Avian influenza IAAP investigations in two areas yielded five wild-bird notifications; all negative, no human cases. Authorities urge reporting abnormal animal behavior and vaccination of pets; seek post-exposure care after bites.

triage.headline_ja: クイアバ市、人獣共通感染症の監視を強化し住民保護のため積極的な監視体制を維持
triage.triage_reason: 定例の環境・疫学サーベイランス報告であり、鳥インフルエンザ・黄熱の検査は全て陰性、狂犬病の人への感染例もなし。異常事態や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 内容は地方自治体による定期的な人獣共通感染症サーベイランス活動報告であり、内臓リーシュマニア症・スポロトリコーシス・狂犬病は地域内で管理されている状況。鳥インフルエンザ・黄熱の検査結果はすべて陰性で新規の公衆衛生上の脅威は確認されていない。

article.articleHeadline: 減肥藥掀服飾革命！諾和諾德新藥挫敗、密西根爆萬人感染 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Weight-loss drugs spark a fashion revolution! Novo Nordisk's new drug setback; Michigan sees tens of thousands infected
article.articleSummary: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are reshaping consumer behavior, with Mounjaro helping a Denver lawyer lose 80 pounds and return to Macy's to shop. Novo Nordisk’s experimental cardiovascular drug ziltivekimab failed to show efficacy in late-stage trials, sending its stock down about 7.3%. In the United States, Michigan reports a cyclosporiasis outbreak with 10,773 confirmed cases and 193 hospitalizations, no deaths yet. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola outbreaks continue in eastern provinces, with Science noting the virus had already been spreading earlier this year. In biopharma and cyber, Amgen confirms a data breach exposing patient health information stored in third-party clouds. Moderna’s quarterly revenue beat expectations thanks to vaccine deals and COVID-19 vaccine sales, and the company awaits a U.S. decision on its influenza vaccine.

triage.headline_ja: 減量薬がファッション革命を巻き起こす！ノボノルディスクの新薬に挫折、ミシガン州で1万人超が感染
triage.triage_reason: 記事は主にGLP-1減量薬やノボノルディスク・Amgen・Modernaに関する経済ニュースが中心で、DRCのエボラ流行については『東部で継続している』という既知情報の言及のみで新規性・詳細情報が乏しい。
triage.notes: 米国ミシガン州のCyclosporiasis集団感染や企業関連ニュースは対象国リスト外・非感染症トピックのため評価対象外。DRCのエボラについては継続中との言及のみで規模・新規性等の詳細不明のためWATCHとした。

article.articleHeadline: Korban Terus Berjatuhan, Ebola di Kongo Kini Tembus 3.500 Kasus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Casualties continue to mount as Ebola in Kongo now surpasses 3,500 cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 3,500 cases, with 3,532 confirmed infections reported as of August 1, 2026. The ministry statement via X reports 807 patients in isolation or hospitalized, 626 recoveries, and 1,556 deaths, yielding a case fatality rate of 44.1%. Contact tracing stands at 78.7%. The news follows WHO’s May 17 declaration of the DRC–Uganda Ebola outbreak as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, reflecting international concern and a very high regional risk of spread. No specific symptoms or infection sources are provided. The report situates the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with WHO highlighting risks of spread in the region.

triage.headline_ja: 犠牲者が増え続ける、コンゴのエボラは現在3,500例を突破
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言済みのDRC-ウガンダ・エボラ流行で3,500例超・致死率44.1%と深刻な影響があり、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダも発生地域として記載されているが対象国リストに含まれず、また記事本文でも詳細な言及がないためverified_locationsにはDRCのみ含めた。WHOはPHEICを既に宣言しており、既存の国際対応枠組みが機能している点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: 母女越南探親返台確診登革熱　未告知旅遊史裁罰1萬
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mother and daughter who visited relatives in Vietnam and returned to Taiwan were diagnosed with dengue fever; did not disclose travel history, fined NT$10,000.
article.articleSummary: Two imported dengue fever cases in Kaohsiung City, Taiwan: a 37-year-old Vietnamese immigrant resident of Dong’anli and her 13-year-old daughter. They visited relatives in Vietnam July 2–24 and returned with fever and myalgia. The mother developed fever July 26, sought care July 29, and was confirmed July 31; the daughter developed fever July 28 and was PCR-confirmed on August 1 after the mother’s diagnosis. The family initially did not disclose travel history, resulting in a NT$10,000 fine under the Infectious Disease Control Act. Both are hospitalized under mosquito isolation. Public health authorities intensified vector control, including home inspections, emergency spraying, and environmental cleanup. Vector surveillance on August 1 found high Aedes density: Xi’anli (60 households; 10 positive containers) and Dong’anli (30 households; 22 positive containers), with positive containers ranging from tires and water barrels to plant pots, gutters, canvas water, and debris; adult Aedes albopictus captured on-site.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナム親族訪問から台湾に帰国した母娘が登革熱と確診、渡航歴未申告で1万台湾ドルの罰金
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における輸入例（ベトナム渡航歴あり）の登革熱2例であり、通常の検疫対応の範囲内で、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 台湾は対象国リストに含まれず、ベトナムは渡航歴として言及されているのみでベトナム国内での発生・流行を主題とした記事ではないため、verified_locationsは空とした。台湾当局によるベクター対策強化（蚊媒介密度調査、緊急消毒等）は通常の対応範囲。
